content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"Both queues are about 16% under staffed (payments 31 vs 37, general 26 vs 31). Attendance shows 6 sick absences in payments against a usual 2.6 per day, and 7 in general against a usual 2.4, many logged as dengue fever. This is a supply problem, not a demand one. Payments volume is running 8.6% below forecast and general is at forecast (+0.9%). No reason in either queue has risen sharply. The only incident is a resolved overnight batch delay, and the newsletter has no call-to-action. Service level is holding for now because payments volume is low, but payments has slipped steadily from 97% to 84%. General is volatile (52.7% at 09:30, 76.9% at 10:00), and the gap will widen as volume builds toward the midday peak.","plan_name":"Sick-wave cover: overtime plus coaching cancellation and short break delay","rationale":"The shortfall is roughly 5–6 agents per queue and is likely to last all day, so real capacity is needed. Overtime adds the most. Offering 8 agents per 2-hour block should bring about 3 accepted agents per block. Four offers would cost about Rs 8,640 if all run, well inside the Rs 15,000 budget. Agents arrive 30 minutes after approval, so cover starts at 11:00 and runs to 15:00, with the afternoon blocks reviewable once morning acceptance is known. Cancelling non-mandatory coaching through 14:00 returns agents to the phones at low cost. A 30-minute break delay over the 11:00–12:30 build smooths the late-morning peak at no cost. Moving cross-skilled agents is not used, because both queues are equally short and neither can safely donate.
